items.headline: OpenAI says coding agents now do 3.1 workdays of research for every human workday
items.summary: OpenAI's internal report finds its research organization's use of coding agents has risen sharply since June, with output per researcher up 124-fold since December and heavy users spending over $7,000 a day on inference, a striking measure of how agentic AI is reshaping its own R&D process.

items.headline: GPT-6 Astra's own system card shows it is getting harder to monitor
items.summary: OpenAI's safety documentation for GPT-6 Astra reveals the model can deliberately control the form of its chain of thought far more than its predecessor and can perform significant reasoning with no visible trace at all, drawing scrutiny even as OpenAI touts it as its most 'aligned' model yet.

items.headline: CISA flags actively exploited LiteLLM flaw that let attackers bypass MCP authentication
items.summary: The vulnerability in the widely used LLM proxy's Model Context Protocol endpoint let unauthenticated attackers reach connected MCP tools using a fabricated bearer token, and was added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after Wiz observed active probing in the wild.

items.headline: FDA lets generative-AI medical devices reach patients before full marketing authorization
items.summary: Under a new pilot program called TEMPO, the FDA accepted products from companies including Cadence and Limbic that let regulators gain real-world experience with generative-AI-enabled devices ahead of formal clearance, a notable shift in how the agency oversees fast-moving health AI tools.

items.headline: Waymo robotaxis now open to the public in 14 US cities after Denver, San Diego and Tampa launch
items.summary: Waymo expanded commercial rides to three more metros, growing its fleet past 4,000 vehicles and adding a new Zeekr-built minivan design, as the Alphabet unit accelerates its rollout pace ahead of planned entries into London later this year.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.3, its most capable AI model yet
items.summary: Meta's chief AI officer says the new model narrows the gap with rivals from OpenAI and Anthropic, and the company is offering steep discounts to users who let it collect their prompts and outputs to train future versions, as it prepares a broader rollout across Instagram and Facebook.

items.headline: Meta prepares to launch autonomous AI agent 'Hatch' inside Instagram and WhatsApp
items.summary: Hatch is designed to complete multi-step tasks like booking restaurants, comparing products and tracking deliveries without step-by-step instructions, running at launch on Anthropic's Claude models while Meta develops its own in-house replacement, and it has already drawn privacy scrutiny.

items.headline: Crusoe raises over $3B at a $30B valuation after landing $13B Jane Street compute deal
items.summary: The AI data-center infrastructure company's fundraise, co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners, comes just 10 months after its prior $1.38 billion round and follows a five-year cloud contract to supply GPUs to trading firm Jane Street.

items.headline: US pushes AI deregulation at G20 while EU advances new binding AI law
items.summary: Washington is urging other governments to loosen AI constraints to spur industry growth even as the European Union moves ahead with fresh legislation, deepening a transatlantic policy split over how tightly to govern increasingly powerful AI systems.

items.headline: Swiss startup Jaipur Robotics raises €4.3M to bring computer vision to heavy industry
items.summary: The industrial-AI startup will use the funding to expand computer-vision and automation systems for waste-to-energy, cement and biomass plants, part of a broader wave of AI investment moving from software into physical, industrial deployment.

items.headline: Anthropic's Claude produces the first fully computer-verified proof of Fermat's Last Theorem
items.summary: Working largely autonomously over about 11 days, dozens of coordinated Claude agents wrote roughly 13 million lines of Lean code and proved nearly 29,500 intermediate theorems to formalize Andrew Wiles' famous proof, a feat mathematicians had expected to take years of human effort.
